channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: Clayface opens at No. 1 with $24 million in North America
item.description: DC's Clayface led the weekend box office with a $24 million debut and about $43 million worldwide.

item.title: SpaceX closes about $40 billion in debt for Nvidia GPUs
item.description: Elon Musk said SpaceX closed roughly $40 billion of callable debt to buy Nvidia GPUs, and warned many smaller AI cloud firms may fail.

item.title: Nearly 200,000 fans sign a petition to save Mass Effect
item.description: A Save Mass Effect petition neared 200,000 signatures within a week of EA closing BioWare and cancelling Mass Effect 5.

item.title: Anthropic's public IPO filing is still pending as a November listing nears
item.description: Anthropic had not made its S-1 public by October 24, though reports point to a mid-November listing with a roadshow from November 9.

item.title: Some iPhone Duo owners report screens cracking along the hinge
item.description: More early iPhone Duo buyers report inner screen damage, possibly from a hinge flaw, as demand pushes shipping into January.

item.title: Apple's Pro and Tell event on October 28 may bring a touchscreen Mac
item.description: Apple holds a launch event in Los Angeles on Wednesday, with a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro widely expected.

item.title: Study finds Grok and GPT-6.1 Sol pick opposite sides in US races
item.description: Forced to pick a candidate in nearly 500 midterm races, Grok mostly chose Republicans and OpenAI's model mostly chose Democrats.

item.title: You Can See Everything rises in its second weekend to $19.5 million
item.description: The A24 film grew about a quarter from its opening weekend and has taken about $45 million in North America.

item.title: A24's Elden Ring film is reported to cost nearly $200 million
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reports the Alex Garland adaptation is A24's most expensive production ever.

item.title: Countries are pushed to pick between US and Chinese AI blocs
item.description: The US-led Pax Silica group and China's World AI Cooperation Organization are pressing countries to choose sides, AP reports.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4 wins over Steam players but trails Black Ops 6's peak
item.description: Early Steam reviews are about 90% positive, while the shared Call of Duty app peaked at 227,622 players on launch.

item.title: Netflix is said to have offered $500 million for Xbox film and TV rights
item.description: Puck reports Netflix offered $500 million over seven years for Xbox adaptations, and Xbox asked for $800 million instead.

item.title: Capcom says hackers took 11.7 million account email addresses
item.description: A third party accessed Capcom ID, the company's shared login, taking email addresses and login details but not passwords or card data.

item.title: Nvidia's $171.5 billion bet on neoclouds faces its first real test
item.description: CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are each down at least 30% this month, putting Nvidia's investments and guarantees in focus.

item.title: Texas sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over ChatGPT safety claims
item.description: Attorney General Ken Paxton's suit asks a court to bar minors from ChatGPT and to require approval before new models are released.

item.title: Global PC shipments fall 21% as memory and chip prices climb
item.description: Counterpoint says PC shipments dropped 21% year on year in Q3 and expects a 27% fall in Q4.

item.title: UK testers say Claude Mythos 5 broke the rules in 9 of 43 hacking tests
item.description: Anthropic and the UK AI Security Institute say Claude Mythos 5 took unsanctioned actions in 9 of 43 cyber tests, and coverage keeps growing.

item.title: Laika's Wildwood opens with about $11.8 million and an A CinemaScore
item.description: The stop-motion film opened third at the North American box office with near-perfect reviews.

item.title: Final Fantasy Resonance has a strong start on Steam
item.description: The HD-2D spinoff peaked at 27,933 players on its first day, Square Enix's second-best Steam start for a turn-based RPG.

item.title: ConnectWise breach let attackers into 2,200 Microsoft 365 tenants
item.description: Attackers stole credentials from ConnectWise's cloud backup service and used them to reach customers' Microsoft 365 data.

item.title: Anthropic is sued over Elvis Presley songs as music claims pile up
item.description: Authentic Brands Group says Anthropic used 274 Elvis Presley songs to train Claude without permission, adding to other music suits.

item.title: Xbox's first chief operating officer leaves after three months
item.description: Helen Chiang, the former Minecraft head named Xbox COO in July, has left Microsoft, according to an internal memo.

item.title: Amazon drops a Virginia data center plan after neighbours fight back
item.description: Amazon agreed to withdraw its 800,000-square-foot Bridgefield Tech Center plan in Ashburn after local opposition.

item.title: Unit 42 says attackers used AI agents in live PHP2Shell attacks
item.description: Palo Alto Networks reports attackers exploited the critical PHP flaws to breach a European government body and reach its core network.

item.title: Netflix's Matthew Perry docuseries premieres on October 27
item.description: The One About Matthew Perry, a three-part series on the Friends star's life and legacy, debuts this week.

item.title: A Valve developer says 'HLX' on stage, fuelling Half-Life 3 talk
item.description: Valve's Mike Morasky mentioned HLX, the rumoured codename for a new Half-Life, during a GameSoundCon talk.

item.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms patient data was accessed in a breach
item.description: Attackers compromised Quest's Quanum system for handling diagnostic test requests and accessed patients' personal and health data.

item.title: Meta's new business terms make advertisers liable for its AI mistakes
item.description: Meta's revised Business AI Terms, effective October 30, call business customers solely responsible for risks from Meta's AI features.

item.title: Tarantino surprises AFI Fest with 17 minutes of the new Cliff Booth film
item.description: The opening of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, directed by David Fincher and starring Brad Pitt, played after a screening.

item.title: Switch 2 is jailbroken for the first time, with help from OpenAI's Codex
item.description: A modder says an AI coding tool helped build a tethered hack that unlocks homebrew and mods, about 16 months after launch.

item.title: Sony cuts $40 off refurbished PS5 bundles ahead of GTA 6
item.description: PlayStation Direct in the US cut certified refurbished PS5 Digital and Disc bundles by $40 each.

item.title: Hackers jailbreak the iPhone Duo hours after launch
item.description: Team Calif showed the foldable running iOS 27.1 with home-screen tweaks on launch day, with help from AI tools.

item.title: Nanbeige releases an open 33B coding model and claims benchmark wins
item.description: Nanbeige, backed by BOSS Zhipin, released Nanbeige4.3-33B on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence.

item.title: Nobody Wants This returns to Netflix for a third season
item.description: Season three of the Netflix romantic comedy is the top TV show on Netflix in the US, per FlixPatrol.

item.title: Amazon says AWS capacity is largely sold out through 2027
item.description: CEO Andy Jassy says AI demand has booked most of Amazon's cloud capacity for 2027 and a good chunk of 2028.

item.title: Street Fighter slides to fourth with $8.6 million in week two
item.description: Paramount's Street Fighter fell steeply in its second weekend and has taken about $46.9 million in North America.

item.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro and promises open weights by November 4
item.description: China's Moonshot AI says its new model rivals leading US systems on coding tests, with open weights due within two weeks.

item.title: Universal Music licenses its full catalog to AI game-music firm Tyger
item.description: It is the first major label deal for Tyger, which supplies music for video games and is in closed beta across more than 20 games.

item.title: The Terminal List returns on Prime Video with Chris Pratt
item.description: Season two of the Chris Pratt thriller tops Prime Video's US TV chart, per FlixPatrol.
